summary.assessment: This run returned no wrong number of consequence: all 5 figures without data were declined with a stated reason, all 42 printed values (B1, B3, C5) are exact, and every value read from geometry that it returned is within 2.7 % of its axis range, most far closer (B2's 90 line points average 0.2 %, C3's 264 stacked segments 0.15 points, C1's bars 0.3 %). Its typical failure is omission, not misreading, and it says so in `uncertain`: it skipped the 90 raw dots behind B2's lines and nulled 4 of B5's 30 medians where the median line lies on a box edge. The remaining measurement error is small and local: the boundary between the two hatched classes of C3's stacked bars (up to 2.7 points, with 0.1-1.1 point slivers in classes that are empty) and a constant +0.05 on C4's bars. The two large penalties in the automatic score are not value errors: B2's series are named 'Smoothed ...' instead of the panel title, and the saved box of C4's panel (a) spans the whole figure, so correct values count as missing plus extra. It can be trusted on every chart kind in this set (printed-label bars and pies, plain bars, interval and forest plots, lines, box plots, stacked bars), provided a consumer reads `uncertain` for what was left out and treats sub-point stacked slivers and edge-coincident box medians as approximate.
